first_impression.reaction: My daughter sent me this, so I read it properly. The opening is sensible and plain, and I liked that it gets to the weather straight away: "the garden that sets the mood is also the venue with the least shelter from the weather." That is exactly what I was going to ask. No silly slang, short paragraphs, easy on the iPad. I'll keep going.

journey.quote: It works when the styling and the backup plan are decided together, because the garden that sets the mood is also the venue with the least shelter from the weather.
journey.reaction: Good. Someone is thinking about rain, not just flowers. That's the practical start I wanted.

journey.section: Real garden weddings from our pages
journey.quote: Eight couples and eight gardens, each described as their own story tells it.
journey.reaction: Lovely for my daughter, but eight of these in a row is a lot of peacocks and fairy lights for me. I skimmed most of it. It doesn't tell me anything about how the day was run or who looked after it.

journey.quote: Put the front rows, and the grandparents, where the shade falls at the hour of the ceremony, with every row on level ground.
journey.reaction: Thank you. Someone remembered the grandparents. My mother would be in one of those front rows.

journey.section: What to plan for with your venue
journey.quote: Each point below ends in questions to ask before you book, and the answers belong in writing.
journey.reaction: This is the sentence I would underline. Answers in writing is how I like to do things.

journey.section: Wet weather plan and covered space
journey.quote: Who makes the call to move under cover, and by what time on the day?
journey.reaction: A very good question. I'd forward this list to my husband as it is.

journey.quote: Where can guests get drinking water outdoors?
journey.reaction: Practical and properly sourced on the sun advice. Older guests in the heat is a real worry for me, and this treats it seriously.

journey.section: Access for older guests and a route without steps
journey.quote: Walk the day as your oldest guest would.
journey.reaction: This is the part written for me. My mother uses a walking frame and these three questions are exactly what I'd ask. I'd have liked one more about where cars can drop people off and somewhere to sit if they can't stand for long.

journey.quote: Who is on the venue's side on the day, and do they stay until the end of the night?
journey.reaction: Good, but if this is overseas, the first thing I want to know is about the money. There's nothing in this list about deposits, the contract, what language it's in or what currency we pay in. That's what keeps me up at night.

journey.quote: How do guests travel between the hotel and the garden, and how long does it take?
journey.reaction: Yes, but can my mother manage that transfer, and how far is a doctor if someone has a fall? Nothing about mobility or medical help abroad.

journey.quote: Through Wedded Concierge, a Wedded Advisor works in your time zone, quotes in AUD and confirms inclusions in writing before you commit.
journey.reaction: Now we're talking. Australian dollars and things in writing before we commit. That is what I'd want to hear.

journey.section: Plan your garden wedding with Wedded Concierge
journey.quote: One Wedded Advisor plans the venue, travel, vendors and payments anywhere in the world as your single point of contact from start to finish, and the fee is agreed in writing before any work begins.
journey.reaction: One person accountable and the fee in writing. That's the most reassuring line on the page. I still don't know who that person is or whether I can speak to them on the phone.

unanswered_questions: Is the deposit protected, and who holds it if we pay through Wedded Concierge?
Who do I ring if something goes wrong at 2am Italian time, and is that the same Wedded Advisor?
Can I speak to someone on the phone before anything is booked?
Will the venue contract be in English, and does the Advisor go through it with us?
Is travel or wedding insurance something the Advisor helps with?
What happens with an elderly guest's mobility or medical needs at a garden abroad?
Who is the Wedded Advisor? A name and a face would help.
would_share_with: My husband, with the venue question lists marked
My daughter, about the access section for her grandmother

cta_reaction.quote: Tell Wedded Concierge the garden you have in mind, your month and how many guests are coming.
cta_reaction.why: The fee in writing, AUD quotes and one point of contact are what I want, so I'd look. But I'd want to know I can ring a real person and that the deposits are safe before I put my details into anything. If the page said how the first conversation happens, I'd be a yes.

top_3_changes: Add deposit, contract language and payment currency questions to the destination list, so the money side is covered for overseas gardens.
Add mobility on transfers and nearest medical help to the destination list.
Add a drop-off point and seating for guests who cannot stand long to the access questions.

suggested_edits.old: - Who is on the venue's side on the day, and do they stay until the end of the night?
suggested_edits.new:
- Who is on the venue's side on the day, and do they stay until the end of the night?
- Who holds your deposits, and what does the contract say if the date or plans change?
- Is the contract in English, and in which currency are payments due?
suggested_edits.why: Deposits and contracts in another language and currency are my biggest fears abroad, and the page never mentions them.

suggested_edits.old: - How do guests travel between the hotel and the garden, and how long does it take?
suggested_edits.new:
- How do guests travel between the hotel and the garden, and how long does it take?
- Is that transfer suitable for guests with limited mobility, and where is the nearest medical help?
suggested_edits.why: Elderly guests abroad are a real concern, and this adds a venue question without claiming anything about the brand.

suggested_edits.old: - Is that route lit after dark?
suggested_edits.new:
- Is that route lit after dark?
- Is there a drop-off point close to the ceremony, and seating for anyone who cannot stand for long?
suggested_edits.why: My mother uses a walking frame. Where the car stops and where she sits matter as much as the steps.
